picks.excerpt: The Godot open-source game engine project has announced it will reject nearly all AI-generated or AI-assisted code contributions, citing concerns about training data provenance, license compliance, and code quality. The policy puts Godot at direct odds with the broader industry trend toward AI-assisted development workflows.

An Electronic Arts executive claims AI tools have produced a genuine creativity surge among game developers, with teams pursuing ideas previously too time-consuming or resource-intensive to attempt. The optimistic framing contrasts sharply with ongoing industry-wide job cuts partly attributed to AI efficiency gains.

Valve has responded to Epic CEO Tim Sweeney's criticism of its AI disclosure policy by making AI-content labels more prominent in Steam search results and demoting AI-assisted games in ranking — and a community modder escalated further with a browser extension that adds unavoidable AI warnings to game pages. The escalating battle is reshaping how storefronts handle AI transparency.
